questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Limit how much you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how much you ride each day.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours a day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tire faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane of traffic.
You will get through the turn faster.
You will keep better control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing at all times when riding.

questions.question: What should riders do about blind spots?

options.text: They don't exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular habit.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: Which of the following is not recommended for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear like long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible when riding.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, you should make sure that your helmet:
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives you the best protection when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no defects.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not make sudden movements, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make sudden movements, if possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of a lane lets a car driver see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this position?

options.text: Most people don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent the use of a side mirror.
Side mirrors should not be used by motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most people don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, it is better to ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stare straight ahead of their motorcycle.
Be unwilling to move to avoid a hazard.
Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds and scan the road ahead of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds and scan the road ahead of their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes to stop.

questions.question: To make it easier for other motorists to see you, you should:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright-colored clothing makes it easier for others to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to:
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most U.S. motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: Wind noise:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Use earplugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is absorbed into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine walls, enters the bloodstream, and reaches the brain quickly.

questions.question: What material gives the best protection in a crash?
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection if you crash. Always wear long pants and a jacket while riding.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Recommended because it blocks the wind.
Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside cars or trucks. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane without noticing.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using the correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When scanning around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
See if you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for potential escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: As you scan for hazards, look for escape routes in intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.
